sections.markdown:
## B — Audience, level and prerequisites: sharing the road: large vehicles, emergency vehicles, traffic stops, the move-over law and slow-moving vehicles
Audience: every first-time South Carolina Class D applicant; traffic stop conduct matters especially to new and young drivers.
Why it matters to a first-timer: what to do when emergency lights appear behind you, from pulling over to keeping your hands on the wheel, is set out here [A04], along with the move-over rule for a stopped emergency vehicle [A07].
Level: a mix of exact values (truck stopping distance, rear no zone length, hill speed, slow-moving vehicle speed) and conduct and scenario judgment.
Prerequisites: the side no zone and commercial vehicle facts from the previous section, which this section continues.

corpus_stability.reason: The South Carolina Driver's Manual prints a single edition line (Revised 06/2024) on its front cover; its disclaimer says legislative and SCDMV policy changes may make some content out of date until the agency incorporates them, and a possibly newer unlinked upload exists on the issuer site (freshness debt in the run jams), so the corpus is treated as revised at most about once a year, bound to the registered snapshot.
